source_snapshot.title: fix(mcp): repair the orphan bookkeeping and the Windows quoting from #400
source_snapshot.body:
An independent review of #400 found that three of its own fixes were wrong, and that two of its tests were written so they could not fail against the defect they claimed to cover. All were reproduced before fixing.

## Three fixes in #400 were wrong

**An orphan settling mid-run released the *running* command's lock.** `releaseHeldLocks` drops every lock the process holds, not the finishing command's — and the guard only asked whether an orphan was in flight, never whether something was running right now. A command abandoned at its timeout, settling part-way through an unrelated `ix map`, deleted that map's lock and reopened the exact window single-flight exists to close. The guard now also requires `activeRun === null`, which the lock-holding command's own `finally` always satisfies, so nothing is stranded.

**A command that never settles was an immortal orphan.** `finished` derives from `work`; if `work` never settles, the entry could never be removed. Everything keyed off it then failed permanently open, for the life of the server:

- `exitCodeIsOurs` stayed false, so **every** later failing command reported `ok: true` — the precise inverse of the misclassification #400 set out to fix.
- `releaseHeldLocks()` never ran again, so the second `ix_map` coalesced — the headline bug of #400, restored.

Membership is now bounded by a grace timer as well as by the command settling. `installServerErrorHandlers` made non-settling commands *more likely*, since an exception that used to end the process is now only logged, which is what made this reachable.

**Staleness by regex both missed and misfired.** `[^"'\s,\]]*` cannot cross a space, so `[local-path] Doe\...\ix.cmd` — the common Windows shape, not the edge one — went on reading as healthy. And allowing a match to start at an interior `/` made it latch onto the `/npm/ix.cmd` suffix of a *live* path, report it stale, and silently rewrite a working registration with no `--force` (plus `doctor` exiting 1 on a healthy machine). The launcher is now read from the parsed entry, so there is nothing to guess; an unreachable path is still not "gone", since only ENOENT counts.

## A quoting hole, and two tests that could not fail

**`quoteForCmd` passed cmd metacharacters through bare.** Its fast path tested only whitespace and quotes, so a path with `&`, `^` or `|` and no space was emitted unquoted. Verified by round-trip against a real `cmd` invocation:

| argument | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `[local-path] | arrives as `[local-path] cmd runs `D\npm\ix.cmd` as a second command | intact |
| `[local-path] | arrives silently as `[local-path] `ok: true` | intact |
| `[local-path] | mangled | intact |

The reachable input is `resolveLauncher()`'s output — the user's own npm prefix path. The predicate is now a whitelist, and `%` joins `"` as unencodable rather than being expanded by cmd behind the quoting's back.

**The two tests that could not fail are replaced.** The `quoteForCmd` fixture contained a space, so it took the quoting branch either way and never exercised the bare path; the stale-launcher fixture used the one path shape the broken regex happened to match. Both now cover the defect.

## Also

- `MISSING_ENTRY` is tied to our own server name, so an unrelated "not found" in a host's output can no longer read as a free name and overwrite the user's server.
- OpenClaw's Windows write is paired with a matching Windows read, so the platform that writes the file also reads it — the asymmetry VS Code was explicitly fixed for.
- The README no longer claims a write path Windows does not take.
- Tests that reach `acquireMapLock` no longer write into the developer's real `~/.ix/locks`.

## Verification

- `typecheck` clean, lint unchanged from baseline (0 errors, same 41 warnings), knip clean.
- 76 tests pass across the three `mcp` suites.
- **All five fixes validated by restoring the defect** and confirming the intended test — not merely the suite — goes red. One of them caught a sixth test that had silently failed to apply and was not in the file at all.

fix(mcp): repair the orphan bookkeeping and the Windows quoting from #400

An independent review of #400 found that three of its own fixes were wrong,

`releaseHeldLocks` drops every lock the process holds, not the finishing

whether something was running right now. A command abandoned at its timeout

reopening the exact window single-flight exists to close. It now also requires
`activeRun === null`, which the lock-holding command's own finally always
satisfies.

**A command that never settled was an immortal orphan.** Nothing else removed
it, so `process.exitCode` stayed distrusted for the life of the server — making
*every* later failure report success, the precise inverse of the bug #400 set
out to fix — and no lock was ever released again. Membership is now bounded by
a grace timer as well as by the command settling.

**Staleness by regex both missed and misfired.** It could not cross a space, so
`[local-path] Doe\...\ix.cmd` — the common Windows shape, not the edge one —
went on reading as healthy; and letting a match start at an interior `/` made

silently rewrite a working registration with no `--force`. The launcher is now
read from the parsed entry, so there is nothing to guess. An unreachable path
is still not "gone": only ENOENT counts.

**`quoteForCmd` passed metacharacters through bare.** Its fast path asked only
about whitespace, so `[local-path] was emitted unquoted; verified by
round-trip that it then arrives as `[local-path] with cmd running `D\npm\ix.cmd`
as a second command, and that `[local-path] arrives silently as `[local-path]
— a wrong launcher written into every host config and reported as success. The
predicate is now a whitelist, and `%` joins `"` as unencodable rather than
being expanded by cmd behind the quoting's back.

Also: `MISSING_ENTRY` is tied to our own server name, so an unrelated "not
found" in a host's output can no longer read as a free name and overwrite the
user's server; OpenClaw's Windows write is paired with a matching Windows read,
so the platform that writes the file also reads it; the README no longer claims
a write path Windows does not take; and the tests that reached `acquireMapLock`
no longer write into the developer's real `~/.ix/locks`.

The two tests that could not fail — a `quoteForCmd` fixture whose space sent it
down the quoting branch either way, and a stale-launcher fixture that avoided
spaces — are replaced with cases that exercise the defect. All five fixes were
validated by restoring the defect and confirming the intended test goes red.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

test(mcp): scope the UNC staleness case to Windows

A UNC path is a network location only on Windows, where stat fails on an
unreachable one with something other than ENOENT — which is the whole point of
the assertion. Everywhere else those backslashes are ordinary filename
characters, the path really is absent, and `stale` is the right answer, so the
test failed on both Linux runners and both macOS runners while passing on
Windows where it was written. Confirmed against Linux directly rather than by
another CI round-trip.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(mcp): stop the grace path releasing a live lock, restore listing staleness

A review of the previous commit found two regressions in it.

**The grace timer released the lock of a command that was still running.**
`forget()` dropped orphan-set membership *and* ran `afterCommand`. On the settle
path that is right; on the grace path the command is by definition still
working, so `releaseHeldLocks()` deleted the single-flight lock of a map still
in progress — a second `ix map` could then take the workspace out from under it,
which is the window single-flight exists to close. `ix_map` gets 120s, so its
grace is 120s: a map overrunning by that much lost its lock mid-run. The same
call reset the read scope mid-ingest, and because the settle path then
short-circuited, it never reset again — leaving the pre-map scope pinned with
nothing left to invalidate it. The grace now only drops membership; settle
always runs `afterCommand`.

**Staleness detection had gone dead for Claude Code, Codex and Gemini.**
Reading the launcher only from a parsed entry left the three hosts that answer
with a rendered table — and the three that record an absolute `ix.cmd` on
Windows — with no launcher at all, so `judge` skipped the check entirely. After
an nvm switch or a moved npm prefix those hosts read as healthy again and
`install` skipped the repair: the exact failure `stale` was added to fix,
restored where it mattered most, and invisible to a suite whose install/doctor
tests inject the registration directly.

The listing row is read again, but anchored to a token boundary and with a lazy
body: the anchor is what stops a match beginning at an interior `/` and latching
onto the `/npm/ix.cmd` suffix of a live path, and the lazy body is what lets it
span `[local-path] Doe\...`. Both faults the first regex had, without giving up
the coverage. Tests now use the real `claude`/`codex`/`gemini` listing shapes,
and the false-positive fixture uses a path that exists, contains a space and
uses forward slashes — without all three it cannot tell the behaviours apart.

Also from the review: openclaw's Windows read goes back through
`openclaw mcp show`, which cmd handles fine and which is the only check that the
shape written there is one openclaw actually reads — pairing it with the file
write traded a loud `not registered` for a silent `already registered`. The
comment on the grace bound now says plainly that its cost lands on a later call
rather than on the abandoned command. And the README no longer implies OpenClaw
is detected by a config directory; it is still detected on PATH.

Validated by restoring each defect and confirming the intended test goes red,
and the timing-sensitive runner suite was run five times over to check it is
not flaky.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(mcp): scope lock release to the command that took the lock

A third review found the previous commit only deferred the lock bug by one tool
call, and introduced a regression of its own.

**Deferred, not fixed.** Removing `afterCommand` from the grace path left the
release guard reading `liveOrphans.size === 0` — and the grace deliberately
removes a still-running command from that set. So the next command to complete
released the abandoned one's lock anyway, mid-run. The set was doing two jobs
with different lifetimes: "this command's exit code is untrustworthy", which
must be bounded, and "this command is still running", which must not be.

Locks are now owned. `single-flight` records which command took each lock and
releases only that command's, so the question stops being global: a command that
overran its timeout keeps the lock it is still using, and a different command
that has genuinely finished still gives its own up. Both directions were broken
before — releasing everything took a running map's lock, and holding everything
back to avoid that stranded a finished map's.

**Regression.** Moving `resetReadScope` to the settle handler alone meant a
command that never settles — the case the grace exists for — never invalidated
at all. It runs on the grace as well now; it is idempotent, so covering both
costs nothing.

**`launcherInText`, third attempt.** Reading the row left to right was the flaw
common to both previous versions: the match began at the first absolute-looking
token and ran forward, so `cmd /c [local-path] — the documented Windows
wrapper form — yielded `/c [local-path] and reported a live launcher dead,
which re-registers with no `--force`. It now anchors on the `ix` end and walks
back to the nearest absolute-path start, so a preceding flag or an earlier path
on the same row cannot be swallowed, and a launcher under `[local-path] Doe\`
is still found. Four wrapper shapes are pinned by tests.

Also: the orphan drain moved from `withLockDir` to a file-level `afterEach`.
Abandoned commands outlive the test that starts them and the runner's state is
module-level, so every later test saw distrusted exit codes and a held lock —
correct behaviour, silently changing unrelated assertions. Under
`--sequence.shuffle.tests` that failed 4 of 6 seeds; all 6 are clean now.

Each fix validated by restoring the defect and confirming the intended test goes
red, and the ownership one checked by mutating single-flight to ignore the owner.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(mcp): stop parsing the launcher out of a listing row

A fourth review found the previous commit reported `[local-path] Files (x86)\...`
as stale: trimming a row's punctuation was applied to every token, including
the interior tokens of a path that had just been split on its own spaces, so
the rejoin produced `[local-path] Files x86)\...` and stat'd nothing. Brackets
and commas in a username did the same. That is the most common path shape on
Windows, and `stale` re-registers with no `--force`, so it silently rewrote
working configs — the exact failure the rewrite existed to remove.

That is four attempts at recovering a path from a rendered table, each broken
on a different shape: stopping at the first space missed `[local-path] Doe`;
scanning forward swallowed a `cmd /c` prefix; walking back from the `ix` anchor
fell to delimiter trimming. The approach is the defect. Table rows are
space-delimited and paths contain spaces; there is no parse that is right.

So it stops parsing. Staleness only ever needed to establish whether the row
records the launcher we would write today, and a row that does contains that
string verbatim, whatever surrounds it. Containment, case-insensitive with
separators normalised. No tokens, no delimiters, no reconstruction — and no
path shape left to get wrong. The parsed-entry path is unchanged, since a
recorded command needs no guessing at all. `resolveLauncher` is memoised
because `doctor` now consults it once per host.

Tests cover every host row format against every launcher shape that has broken
an attempt — spaces, `(x86)`, brackets, a comma, a wrapper prefix, quotes — in
both directions, which the previous one-directional set did not.

Also from the review: the lock-owner resolver no longer falls back to
`activeRun`. For output that fallback only narrows the damage, but an owner
guessed wrong for a lock means a *different* command's settle deletes a lock
still in use; unattributed is the safe direction. Two comments describing
mechanisms this PR removed are corrected, and the test drain drops from 500ms
to 250 — it was costing ~11s on one file for no coverage.

Every fix validated by restoring the defect, including reinstating the whole
parsing approach to confirm the `(x86)` case goes red. 8/8 shuffle seeds clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(mcp): drop launcher staleness for the CLI-listed hosts, and make --force work

A fifth review found the containment check regressed the case it was meant to
protect, and that the repair it feeds could not land on the flagship host
anyway. Both were demonstrated against the real `claude` and `codex` binaries.

**The regression.** `run()` decodes host output as UTF-8, but a Windows console
emits the OEM code page, so `where ix` returns a non-ASCII npm prefix mangled.
The row holds the real path and `expected` holds the mangled one, so a working
registration read as stale — and `install` then overwrote a config the user had
repaired by hand with a launcher that cannot start, no `--force` required. That
is the failure the previous commit said it existed to remove, reached by a
different road.

**The repair could not land.** `claude mcp add` refuses a name that already
exists and has no force flag. Seeding an isolated Claude config and running the
real `runInstall` gave `outcome: failed`, note `"MCP server ix-memory already
exists in user config"`, config unchanged — for a stale entry *and* for a
foreign one under `--force`. So `--force` was inert for Claude Code, which the
README advertises.

Staleness from a rendered listing row is therefore gone rather than fixed
again. Five attempts, five variants of the same failure: a working registration
called stale, which re-registers without `--force`. A moved npm prefix on
Claude Code, Codex and Gemini is now a manual `ix mcp install --force`. That is
a real gap, and a smaller one than silently rewriting configs that were fine.
Hosts whose config we read directly keep it: there the recorded command is
exact, and the repair is a file write that works.

`--force` is fixed independently, since it was broken for conflicts too:
`register` now takes whether it is replacing something, and hosts whose `add`
will not overwrite clear the name first. Verified against the real `claude`
binary — a foreign registration under `--force` now yields `registered` with
the entry replaced, where before it was `failed` with the entry untouched.

The launcher-shape test matrix goes with the feature it covered; the removal
argv is pinned instead, because the wiring is only observable against a host
binary CI does not have.

Six mutations caught by the intended test, 10/10 shuffle seeds clean.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

revert(mcp): drop the remove-then-add force repair

A sixth review reproduced, against the real `claude` and `codex` binaries, that
the previous commit's `--force` repair can destroy a third-party registration:
`remove` runs, `add` then fails, and the user's server is gone with no backup
and no message saying so. It emptied a seeded `config.toml` — env secret and
all — and a seeded `.claude.json`. The trigger used was an npm prefix containing
`%`, which `run()` deliberately refuses, but any add failure does it: a `"` in
the path, a host CLI error, the 20s timeout, Ctrl-C between the two spawns. I
hit a real transient of that class during the review itself.

The behaviour it replaced was a *bug* — `--force` was inert for Claude Code —
but a safe one: it reported `failed` and left the config untouched. Trading a
safe failure for a destructive one is worse, and fixing it properly needs the
existing definition captured and restored, which is its own change with its own
risks. It was never one of the fifteen findings this branch exists to fix, so
it goes back out rather than getting a seventh iteration here.

The same review also found the remedy this branch documents for the CLI-listed
hosts does not work: `outcomeFor` returns `already-registered` for `ours`
whatever `--force` says, so a moved launcher there is not repairable through
`ix mcp install` at all. The user has to clear the name with the host's own
command first. The README and the code comment now say that instead of
promising `--force`.

Also dropped: the test asserting the removed listing-staleness, which passed
with the feature present or absent — it called `classifyListing` with one
argument, while the removed mechanism was driven by a second. A test that
cannot fail is worse than no test, and the behaviour it aimed at is not
observable at the seams this module exposes.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
